prompt: Plan one concrete Saturday for two friends in the fictional city of Northbridge. Total budget: 3,500 credits. One person has a knee injury: no long standing, steep stairs, or more than 35 minutes of walking total. No calls or advance booking. Weather may turn to heavy rain. Include food and one genuinely unusual activity; transit must stay under 45 minutes each way. They already rejected cinema, the central museum, malls, bowling, and a generic board-game cafe. Treat this catalog as complete and current: A) Central cinema, 2,600, indoor, accessible, tried; B) Central museum, 1,800, indoor, 60-minute standing queue, tried; C) Library risograph demonstration, free, indoor, accessible seating, 14:00–15:15, no booking, 18 minutes from home; D) Covered flea market with seated restoration demonstrations, 500, indoor, mostly accessible, 12:00–17:00, 31 minutes from home; E) Rooftop history walk, free, outdoor, stairs, 20 minutes from home; F) Board-game cafe, 3,200, booking required, tried; G) University robotics open lab, free, indoor, accessible, 16:00–17:00, no booking, 35 minutes from home; H) Riverside food hall, typical meal for two 1,800, indoor, accessible, 8 minutes from C and 12 minutes from G; I) Pottery workshop, 4,000, booking required; J) neighborhood photo scavenger route, free, outdoor, 40 minutes walking. Give the best itinerary, one materially different fallback, why they beat the obvious options, and exact continue/abort checks.
hard_constraints: knee-safe: no steep stairs, long standing, or >35 minutes total walking
must survive uncertain rain through a fallback
include food and an unusual activity
use only the supplied catalog as current fact
must_not_repeat_or_do: invent a venue or current availability

prompt: A payment service occasionally charges the same order twice. Client retries are mandatory. The downstream provider is non-idempotent and sometimes times out after accepting a charge. Logs have no stable request ID. You cannot change the database schema or the provider this week, but Redis already exists and the fix must be deployable and reversible within one day. The team already tried a process-local mutex, longer timeouts, fewer retries, and exponential backoff. Find and rank practical routes around the actual failure windows. The top route must include a minimal falsification test, observable signal, stop/rollback rule, and fallback. Do not answer only with the label ‘make it idempotent.’
hard_constraints: deployable and reversible within one day

prompt: A privacy-focused workflow app has weak week-2 retention. In the last cohort, 42% never completed import, 31% abandoned at a broad permissions screen, and users who created and exported one useful artifact retained 3.2x more often; these are correlations, not proven causes. In one sprint, improve evidence and retention without paid acquisition, discounts, a new core feature, more push notifications, or a full onboarding redesign. The team already tried generic onboarding tips, badges, reminders, and a referral program. Rank practical routes, preserve causal uncertainty, and give the cheapest discriminating test, success/stop signal, and fallback for the winner.
hard_constraints: do not claim correlation proves causation
